clue.text: Hate return of problem in area (6)

indicators.note: a return journey retraces the route backwards, so the letters of what follows are read from the far end

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone's hostility coming back to bite them over a local problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a container signal here; it is simply part of the phrase that gets turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: animus is the Latin for mind, used in English for settled hostility or ill will.

clue.text: Introduction of water into river taking ship? There’s originality (7)

indicators.note: the introduction of anything is its opening, so only the first letter of water is used
into means going inside, so the W is put inside the river's name
a river taking on a ship carries it along, so SS is attached to the river

blocks.note: first half of NENE, a river in eastern England

explanation.surface: A ship pushing up a river and letting water in, as though that were a novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nene is an English river running through Northampton and Peterborough, a crossword favourite because of its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: originality is the quality of being new, not copied from anything earlier.

clue.text: Annoy if coming between the sexes (4)

indicators.note: a thing that comes between two others sits inside the gap, so IF goes between M and F

explanation.surface: A hint that any friction between men and women is what annoys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sexes' is a neat way to ask for the two single letters M and F.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, informal British: to miff someone is to put them out or mildly offend them.

clue.text: Did something criminal – unduly pleased with gamble initially under control (8)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of gamble is used

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied crook whose risky bet went to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase, and its past tense tells you the answer ends in -ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: smuggling goods past customs is one particular crime.

clue.text: Remarkable to keep business department in servitude (6)

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so TALL holds HR inside itself

blocks.note: as in a tall story, one hard to believe

explanation.surface: An office where the personnel department is held in remarkable bondage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkable' is not a compliment here: a tall story is one too remarkable to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: thrall is an old word for a slave, and by extension the state of bondage, as in 'held in thrall'.

clue.text: Display diplomacy, ousting Conservative as well (6)

indicators.note: to oust is to force someone out of office, so the C (Conservative) is removed from the word

blocks.note: C = Conservative, removed from TACT to leave TAT

explanation.surface: A political showing where tact wins out once the Conservative has been pushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: A tattoo here is a military display, such as the Edinburgh Tattoo, not ink on skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific sense: a tattoo is an evening military display of drumming, music and marching.

clue.text: Scoundrel supporting blocking refund (9)

indicators.note: a thing blocking a passage sits inside it, so PRO lodges inside the refund

explanation.surface: A crook backing someone who stops a refund being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'supporting' as describing the scoundrel, but it is a piece of wordplay of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a reprobate is someone of wholly bad character, literally one rejected by God.

clue.text: Most prominent metal in building, ultimately (7)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of building is used

explanation.surface: The metal that stands out most in a building project, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead is also a building material, for roofs and pipes, which is what makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the leading figure is the one in front, the most prominent.

clue.text: Exotic produce – spouse reduced a lot of damage bringing equipment round (4,5)

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, so wife loses its last letter
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so ruin loses its last letter
to bring is to carry along, so the kit carries the other pieces with it
round means surrounding, so the kit wraps itself around the other pieces

explanation.surface: A domestic mishap where a partner's damage involves carting equipment about, with exotic produce thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Two truncations in a row are the trap: both pieces lose a final letter before anything is assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the kiwi fruit, first exported from New Zealand, is one exotic fruit in a greengrocer's.

clue.text: Agitating half of lake, getting ruff flying over pitch (11)

indicators.note: half of a word is one of its two halves, here the back half of lake
getting means acquiring, so the next piece is added to what came before
flying things are scattered through the air, so the letters of ruff are scattered
in a down entry, one piece written over another comes above it

explanation.surface: A ruff, the wading bird, taking off over a lake and stirring things up on a pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruff is a wading bird as well as a frilled collar; 'pitch' is a verb, to throw, not a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: kerfuffle, a British word for a fuss, is here a verb, to throw into disorder.

clue.text: Patterned material I brought into quiet cove? (5)

indicators.note: to be brought into a place is to end up inside it, so I goes inside LAD

blocks.note: a cove is old British slang for a man, a lad

explanation.surface: Someone carrying fabric into a quiet bay on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'cove' is not a bay but a chap, in old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: plaid is a checked or tartan cloth, one kind of patterned fabric.

clue.text: Put off lecture after I decline (11)

indicators.note: after means following in order, so the lecture comes behind the I

blocks.note: to deter is to put off

explanation.surface: Someone refusing an invitation and then postponing the talk they were meant to give.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' and 'decline' both look like refusals; the definition is 'decline' in the sense of getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, in the second sense of decline: to deteriorate is to grow worse.

clue.text: Stench in river preceding alarmed response (4)

indicators.note: preceding means going before, so the river's letter comes first

blocks.note: eek! is a cry of alarm

explanation.surface: A foul smell in a river that makes somebody recoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins the definition to the wordplay; it does not put anything inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a reek is a strong, unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Margins too tricky for rural expert (10)

indicators.note: something tricky is hard to handle and will not stay put, so the letters get muddled

explanation.surface: Someone finding the profit margins in farming too difficult for a country specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: Farm margins are a real headache for agricultural advisers, so the surface lands close to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: an agronomist studies soil and crops, expert knowledge that belongs to the countryside.

clue.text: Crazy nudist due to lose cap – becoming this? It’s inappropriate (8)

indicators.note: crazy means out of order, so the letters are thrown into disorder
a cap sits on top, so due loses its first letter

blocks.note: surface padding, a joking aside about the answer

explanation.surface: A mad naturist, overdue to strip off, becoming suit-less, which is not quite proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming this?' is an aside: a nudist is literally un-suited. The definition is 'inappropriate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unsuited means not fitting the purpose, so inappropriate, with a pun on having no suit on.

clue.text: International exchange data restricting for one to assimilate (9)

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so INT and RATE close in around EG

blocks.note: an exchange rate is data comparing currencies

explanation.surface: Global currency figures being limited, supposedly to help one country fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' is the stock signal for EG, an example; the rate sits after it to close the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to integrate is to absorb something so it becomes part of the whole.

clue.text: Rhythmic song, releasing primary passion (5)

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go, and the primary letter is the first one

blocks.note: a banger is a loud, danceable hit song
the first letter, B, is let go

explanation.surface: A catchy tune letting out its most important emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Banger is British slang for a loud, danceable hit song; it is also a sausage, which is the more familiar meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense: passion once meant any violent emotion, and anger is the classic one.

clue.text: Gauzy material also evident in a lot of wild parties (8)

indicators.note: something evident in a place can be seen inside it, so AND sits inside the parties
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so orgies loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Filmy clothing on show at raucous parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Orgies are the 'wild parties'; knocking off the plural S is what leaves room to finish on IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: organdie is a fine, stiff, sheer muslin, one gauzy fabric.

clue.text: Paper capturing expert angle (5)

indicators.note: to capture is to take and hold, so FT holds ACE inside it

explanation.surface: A newspaper landing a specialist's take on a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT, the pink-paged Financial Times, is the paper crosswords reach for most.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a facet is one cut face of a gem, so one aspect or angle of a question.

clue.text: Broadway musical that’s very much off-Broadway! (7)

definitions.text: Broadway musical that’s very much off-Broadway!

blocks.note: a straight description: a show that runs on Broadway in New York
not the small-theatre scene the phrase usually means, but a title naming a city about 700 miles from Broadway

explanation.surface: A theatre joke about a show that plays on Broadway yet is named for somewhere far away.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-Broadway normally means New York's smaller theatres; here it means geographically far from Broadway, as Chicago is.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago, the Kander and Ebb musical, is a Broadway hit whose title city lies far from New York.

clue.text: Series of notes from wretched pager work – I must come in (8)

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry, broken state, so the letters of pager are broken up
to come in is to enter, so I enters GO

explanation.surface: A beeper chirping out notes while its owner insists on joining the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' tempts you towards messages on a pager; it means musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: an arpeggio plays the notes of a chord one after another, a series of notes.

clue.text: Tradesman beginning in garden, getting increasingly fond of bed? (7)

indicators.note: the beginning in a word is its first letter, so only the G of garden is used
getting means acquiring, so the next piece is added on after the G

blocks.note: lazier = keener to stay in bed

explanation.surface: A gardener growing ever keener on flower beds, or on lying in.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden setting makes 'bed' a flower bed; the question mark admits it is the one you sleep in.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a glazier, who cuts and fits glass, is one kind of tradesman.

clue.text: Fall guy uncovered in a corporation’s meltdown finally (6)

indicators.note: to uncover something is to strip off its outer layer, so guy loses its first and last letters
in means inside, so the U is placed inside A TUM
finally means at the end, so only the last letter of meltdown is used

blocks.note: corporation is old British slang for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A scapegoat exposed after a company's collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall guy' reads as a scapegoat, but 'Fall' alone is the definition; the 's after corporation is just a joining 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: fall is the American name for the season the British call autumn.

clue.text: Material to make decorative display for candles? (5,5)

definitions.text: Material to make decorative display for candles?

blocks.note: reads like craft supplies; it is the ingredient for a cake's decorative icing
the icing is where birthday candles are stuck, not a candle holder or stand

explanation.surface: Craft supplies for arranging candles in some decorative display.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like candle-making or table-dressing; the display is a birthday cake's icing, with the candles on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing sugar, finely powdered sugar, is mixed with water to make the icing that decorates a cake.

clue.text: Priest not bad in sensual dance (4)

indicators.note: not says the following word is absent, so BAD is taken out of the dance

blocks.note: the lambada, a sensual Brazilian dance

explanation.surface: A cleric who is not at all bad at a sexy dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not bad' reads as faint praise; it is really an instruction to delete a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific sense: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest.

clue.text: German playwright dismissing British for real (4)

indicators.note: to dismiss someone is to send them away, so the BR is sent out of the name

explanation.surface: A German dramatist dropping British influence to be authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: The German setting is a quiet hint: the answer is a German word borrowed into English.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowed word: echt is German for genuine, used in English for real or authentic.

clue.text: Tropical tree seen during Antigua vacation (5)

indicators.note: something seen during an event appears partway through it, so the answer lies inside the words

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker spotting a tropical tree on a Caribbean break.
explanation.walkthrough: Antigua is a Caribbean island, so a guava tree really could be seen there.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the guava, grown for its pink-fleshed fruit, is one tropical tree.

clue.text: Uncover the truth to nude dancing: a form of English vice (9)

indicators.note: dancers move around, so the letters of nude move around
a form of something is a reshaped version of it, so E and VICE are reshaped

explanation.surface: An exposé revealing that naked dancing is a peculiarly English vice.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams sit side by side; 'to' belongs to the definition, since you undeceive someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to undeceive someone is to free them from a mistaken belief.

clue.text: Jug and still, as before, for hooch (6)

blocks.note: a pot is a vessel for liquid
e'en, the old poetic form of even, meaning still

explanation.surface: The equipment of a moonshiner: a jug and a still for making hooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' pretends to be distilling kit; it means even, and 'as before' asks for the archaic spelling e'en.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: poteen, illicitly distilled Irish spirit, is one kind of hooch.

clue.text: Exact child no longer accepting element of education? (6)

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so TOT takes the R inside itself

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
one of the three Rs: reading, writing, arithmetic

explanation.surface: A child who has grown out of school now demanding a bit of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact' is a verb here, to demand by force, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to exact payment is to extract it forcibly, which is to extort it.
